title: Operator runbook and burn-rate slab for incremental deploys
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: PRD + runbook to formalize a slab-based error-budget replenishment model and an operator playbook for incremental model/runtime deploys. Goal: give on-call engineers deterministic, measurable actions for staged rollouts and rapid fallbacks when tenant burn-rate or tail-latency exceed defined slabs. This ticket clarifies scope (SLO definition + operator procedures + canary exit automation knobs). Implementation (automated enforcement and telemetry) is out of scope but listed as dependencies. The doc must: (1) define slab tiers with quantitative thresholds across p50/p95/p99 and availability, (2) specify short/medium burn windows and replenishment math, (3) create operator runbook steps for detection, manual shunt and rollback, and (4) define canary probe criteria, golden prompt sets and automated exit gates for canary traffic.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Slab matrix published with at least four tiers (Green/Amber/Red/Critical) that map to specific numeric SLOs for p50/p95/p99 latency and availability per workload class.

A2: Burn-rate definition: document demonstrates how error-budget is consumed over 5m, 1h, 6h windows and shows replenishment formula (linear drip + admin credit) with worked examples for a 7-day rolling window.

A3: Canary exit gates defined: minimum probe QPS, golden prompt pass-rate >= 98% for fidelity checks, p99 latency delta threshold <= 20% relative to baseline, and error-burst detection rule (burst multiplier > 4x baseline) that triggers automatic canary hold.

A4: Operator runbook sections cover detection (alerts + dashboards), graduated mitigation actions (throttle, tenant-shunt, scale-up, circuit-breaker), and forensic checklist for post-mortem; each action maps to slab tiers.
A5: Acceptance test doc with synthetic scenarios (slow tail, error burst, regional plateau) and expected operator action validated in a staging drill (date scheduled).
A6: Links to downstream implementation tickets (ENG) enumerated and reviewed by infra/serving leads.
A7: PM and on-call eng sign-off recorded in comments and PRD linked in ticket.
checklist: Draft slab matrix and numeric thresholds

notes: This ticket is intended to standardize operator behavior across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. The runbook emphasizes explicit human + automated handoff points to avoid ambiguous rollback decisions. The slab approach aims to balance fast recovery (aggressive canary hold) with minimizing false positives (replenishment math and multiple windows).
runbook_excerpt: If slab==Red and burn-rate(window=5m) > 3x baseline: 1) Pause canary; 2) Trigger tenant-prioritized shunt for affected tenants; 3) Increase autoscale by one step if capacity constrained; 4) If error-rate remains elevated after 10m, roll back to previous model version and open incident with severity assessment.
